text:
incident-bot: :pager: P1 - elevated 5xx on /v1/generate (us-west-2). queue_depth spike >1000. initial detection triggered autoscaling activity.

Ava: I'm on it. seeing repeated 502/504s at the API gateway, paging infra. who can pull GPU pool metrics and HPA events?

Sam: pulling k8s events + pool metrics now. early notes: HPA is reacting to CPU/memory only; queue-length is collected separately (batch only). queue_depth=1035 at 03:41UTC and sustained.

Priya: runtime note: cold warmup for hot models is long. synchronous KV populate is blocking; observed ~110-180s per replica from driver start to readiness in traces.

Liam: pool-manager logs snippet:
2026-03-15T03:41:58Z pool-manager INFO pool=prod-gpu available=0 total=64 allocating=8
2026-03-15T03:43:30Z scheduler ERROR assign failed request_id=abc reason="no free device"

Ava: customer impact: enterprise routes seeing timeouts >20s and 5xx. support already has multiple tickets. need immediate mitigations. options: fallback to smaller model, open burst capacity, or throttle non-essential traffic.

Marta: drafting customer status; need to know mitigation choice to include in note.

Sam: quick mitigations I'll apply: 1) enable routing fallback to a smaller model for non-SLA tenants, 2) enable soft-throttle to reject large batch/ingest requests. will roll routing change in ~2m.

Priya: I'll push a hotfix to make KV populate async and prioritize lanes with queued requests. target deploy ~12m; in internal tests async reduces readiness to ~60-80s.

Jian: curious why HPA didn't prevent this capacity gap. do we expose queue depth as a scaler input?

Sam: current HPA config: metrics = cpu_utilization, memory. we have a separate autoscaler for batch worker queue_length, but model-servers lack queue signal. plus HPA cooldowns are tight so scale-down happened when cpu dipped while warmups were blocked. k8s event fragments:
03:40 HPA scaleUp desired=0->4 reason="cpu" averageUtil=14
03:43 HPA scaleUp desired=4->8 reason="cpu"
03:45 HPA scaleDown desired=8->3 reason="cpu"  # cpu dropped due to blocked warmup
metrics: 03:41 queue_depth=1035

Liam: confirms scale-down occurred while replicas still initializing, causing an allocation hole.

Ava: hypotheses to track in RCA:
- H1: HPA lacks queue_depth / GPU readiness signal and so scale decisions are misaligned with actual serving capacity.
- H2: KV populate is synchronous and long; replicas are not available until ~2-3 minutes after creation.
- H3: aggressive scale-down cooldowns and lack of pre-warmed pool cause oscillation under sudden bursts.

Sam: mitigation executed at 03:50UTC: enabled fallback routing + soft-throttle. immediate observed effects:
- queue_depth: 1035 -> 480 within 6 minutes
- 5xx rate decreased ~65%
- GPU pool still near 100% utilization but fewer allocation failures

Liam: long-term recommendations (ops + infra):
- expose queue_depth metric to HPA for model-server deployment target
- add scale-down inhibition when queue_depth > threshold (e.g., 200)
- create configurable warm_pool of pre-warmed replicas with KV primed
- add burst_reserved capacity toggle to allow emergency allocation for SLA tenants

Priya: runtime follow-ups: implement async KV populate + prioritized KV priming for hot lanes, and validate that readiness drops to ~60-80s; design rollout to avoid thundering-herd by staggering priming. scheduling controlled load replays to quantify.

Jian: action items and owners:
- add queue_length -> HPA & adjust cooldowns: Sam
- pre-warm pool + burst config: Liam
- async KV warmup + populate prioritization: Priya
- short-term policy defaults (fallback/throttle): Sam + Ava
- customer comms + severity tracking: Marta

Ava: I'll open the incident ticket and start the RCA skeleton. handoff plan: I'll hand to night oncall @Liam in 40m. if anything spikes page infra directly.

Sam: created INC-20260315-2943 and attached HPA events, pool logs, and warmup traces.

Priya: note for RCA testing: will run load replay with a pre-warmed pool vs fresh replicas and correlate queue_depth and HPA events to validate H1/H2.

Marta: customers updated; included note about fallback and ETA for fixes. pinging enterprise customers with potential SLA exposure.

Ava: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in place. status: partially mitigated (non-SLA tenants recovered), SLA routes still showing elevated latency. next update scheduled in 30m or earlier if regression. handing off to @Liam for night watch.

Liam: acknowledged. standing watch on GPU pool, will coordinate burst capacity if needed and start drafting a runbook for scale-down cooldowns.

Sam: short-term change: restrict aggressive scale-down while queue_depth > 200. leaving this guard in place for 24h and scheduling proper rollout with unit tests.

Ava: thanks all for quick coordination. closing operational channel for this incident; RCA work and follow-ups will continue in INC-20260315-2943.
